translation_notes: `@graph self.graph` (an attribute as the graph), the two `self.graph.triples((x, None, None))` comprehensions become `m{ {self.__identifier} ?p ?o }` and `m{ ?s ?p {self.__identifier} }`, the removals `-{ {self.__identifier} {p1} {o1} }` / `-{ {s1} {p1} {self.__identifier} }`. The two `self.graph.remove` loops remove fully specified triples read just before, so there is no wildcard to write and the loops stay (the whole set could be `-{ {id} ?p ?o }` + `-{ ?s ?p {id} }`, but that is a rewrite, not a notation change); the stratum's `-{ s p ?o }` wildcard is therefore not exercised. An interpolated blank node is matched as that node, not as a wildcard, verified (fixture has blank nodes as object, subject and identifier).

`self.graph.addN([(i, p1, o1, self.graph) for ...])` has no island for a list of statements: it becomes a loop of `+{ {i} {p1} {o1} }`, one add per statement -- the minor restructuring. `compute_qname` is left as is; the unused `@prefix rdf/rdfs` of the draft were dropped (they would bind rdf/rdfs on the caller's graph through @graph, for nothing).

`self.__identifier` is not name-mangled: the region is extracted as a module-level function. Driver: `self` is a SimpleNamespace(graph, __identifier, qname), graph parsed from fixture.ttl per side, compared as an argument after the call (graph by isomorphism, qname). Calls: full rename (statements out, in, a self-loop, blank nodes), identity (no-op), a node without statements (zero solutions), rename to a blank node, a blank node as the old identifier, an IRI for which compute_qname fails, None (`assert i`). The fixture has a neighbour with another statement on the same (subject, predicate). Mutants killed: in-removal widened to a wildcard, any of the four loops removed, in-read widened.
optimization_notes: optimized.py: the two reads become `list(self.graph.predicate_objects(id))` and `list(self.graph.subject_predicates(id))`; the two removal loops, which removed exactly the triples just read (every triple with the old node as subject, then as object), become two wildcard removes `self.graph.remove((id, None, None))` / `((None, None, id))`; the two addN become `self.graph += [...]` (Graph.__iadd__ is the same addN with the graph as context). Order kept: read, remove, rebind __identifier, add out then in (the self-loop case depends on it). `assert i`, the BNode test and the bare try/except are kept.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph self.graph`, `list(m{ {self.__identifier} ?p ?o })` / `list(m{ ?s ?p {self.__identifier} })`, the wildcard removes `-{ {self.__identifier} ?p ?o }` / `-{ ?s ?p {self.__identifier} }` (the stratum's wildcard, which the translation could not use without refactoring), and one `+{ }` loop per list (157 tokens, against 165 with the Python `self.graph += [...]` kept).
No exception to the symmetry rule: the wildcard removal is carried by both sides; only the bulk add differs, each side taking its shortest form.
header_optimization_notes: Python and LD Python: the parenthesised seven-name rdflib import becomes `from rdflib import BNode`, the only name the region uses; the two headers are identical.
